c.tagline: Poland's western cradle — where clockwork goats butt heads and a croissant crowns a saint.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard; booking through an app (Bolt, Free Now or iTaxi) is usually cheaper and easier than a street hail.

emergency.note: 112 is the pan-European emergency number reaching police, fire and ambulance; operators generally speak English.

hood_landmark.Stare Miasto (Old Market Square): Poznań Old Market Square Stary Rynek

avoid.reason: Late-night rowdiness around Stary Rynek bars and occasional pickpockets at the main train station deserve normal awareness.

hood_desc: The Renaissance core around the Old Market Square (Stary Rynek), famed for its colourful merchant houses, the ornate Town Hall whose mechanical goats butt heads at noon, and a ring of restaurants and bars; the natural walkable base for first-timers.

Poznań's trendiest district just northwest of the centre, a grid of restored tenements packed with independent cafes, bistros, bars and the lively Rynek Jeżycki market; best for a hip, local, going-out crowd.

A dignified residential district south of the centre around the Łazarz market hall and the historic Poznań International Fair grounds (MTP), with wide streets and Art Nouveau tenements; a calm base close to the action.
A regenerated former working-class district anchored by the vast Stary Browar arts-and-shopping centre in a converted brewery, with parks and a growing café scene; up-and-coming and good value.

The green eastern reach of the city built around Lake Malta, with its regatta course, year-round ski slope, thermal baths and Nowe Zoo; best for families and travellers wanting recreation and open water.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though some locals prefer bottled for taste.

transit.pay: Tickets run on time (from a short 15-minute ticket) rather than distance; buy them from onboard machines, kiosks, or the jakdojade/mPay/moBILET apps and validate on boarding. Contactless bank cards can be tapped on many vehicles. A short-time ticket costs about 4 PLN (~$1.10) and a 24-hour ticket about 15 PLN (~$4).
transit.hours: Trams and buses run about 5am–11pm, after which night lines take over across the city.

bus: Poznań Główny Bus Station (PKS, at the main railway station)

transit.m: MPK bus 159 to Poznań Główny railway station, ~25 min
MPK bus 222 to Rondo Kaponiera / centre, ~20 min

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving about 10% for good service in restaurants is appreciated. State the total you want to pay when handing over money, as simply saying 'thank you' can be taken to mean 'keep the change'.
